notes.English_account: The page continues a discussion of recovering a homotopy type from cohomological information. It lists the fundamental group, the coefficient category or categories, cohomology functors on coefficients with exact-sequence structure, and cup products tied by formal properties. It then proposes the derived-category language, complexes with locally constant cohomology, triangulated structure, derived tensor and possibly derived Hom as a more satisfactory candidate. The writer explicitly says he does not know whether those data recover the homotopy type, then expresses confidence in taking the construction into the nonabelian setting with the (n+1)-category of locally constant n-champs for every n. The sentence is unfinished on this page.

mais par contre n'ai guère de doute qu'en allant au bout de la ``linéarisation''
notes.page_date_title_evidence: Author number 38 is at the upper centre. Archive pencil 183 is in the lower left margin in a separate hand. No date, title, salutation, closing or signature occurs on this sheet. The lower-case opening and unfinished final sentence are directly visible continuation features.
notes.mathematical_reading_risks: The argument made the endings of coefficient words, the cohomological replacement, and the triangulated adjective consequential; none was repaired from agreement. The second insertion is visibly aux even though a smoother construction could suggest another preposition. The derived symbols were read from their strokes, Hom was not underlined, and the detached lower tensor point was kept outside mathematical notation. The local n+1 and n signs were read without changing them to fit a preferred formulation.
notes.mathematical_checks: No mathematical proof, re-proof, computation, formal certificate, or deduction was attempted. check_events is intentionally empty. Reading the argument and the assertion is not recorded as checking its truth.
notes.paragraph_decision: The manuscript is transcribed as one continuous paragraph. L9 starts with a capital but has ordinary spacing and no new indentation, and L8 ends near the right margin.
notes.nontext_mark_policy: Six small nontext sites (seven point/stroke components in total) are reproduced as TikZ marks at approximate text anchors. Their physical presence is distinguished from their uncertain origin or authorship. The pale diffuse grey spot near (836,1773) and ordinary copy grain are not promoted to manuscript ink.
